html:
A collection of Roman recipes in Latin, probably put together in the late 4th or 5th century from older material. It is often called the oldest surviving cookbook in Europe. It takes its name from Marcus Gavius Apicius, a famous gourmet in the time of Tiberius, though he did not write it.

The ten books are sorted by kind of dish: sauces, vegetables, meat, birds, seafood and so on. Recipes rarely give amounts or times. They show a cuisine that loved strong mixed flavours: fish sauce in almost everything, honey and vinegar, and herbs such as lovage and rue. They also use a lot of black pepper from India, brought by the trade that sent Roman ships to Muziris.

The text survives in two 9th-century manuscripts from monasteries in Fulda and Tours. Its Latin is close to everyday speech, so it also helps scholars of the language.
